cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: === A. THE FAMOUS ONE EVERYONE WANTS TO PARTNER WITH ===
A very well-known HR brand — 58/100 · No
Not a fit. No named person who can say yes and do the work.
Audience overlap           13/40  weak  — A famous logo with no audience overlap brings attention, not buyers.
Ease of working together    3/10  weak  — Partnerships die in the gap between agreeing and executing.
! No named person who can say yes and do the work.
· Well known, weak overlap — this is the fame trap. Attention, not buyers.
· Guessed rather than known: how much of their list is actually mid-market. A score built on a guess is worse than no score — ask them.
=== B. THE SMALL ONE WITH A PERFECT OVERLAP ===
A mid-market onboarding consultancy — 92/100 · Start here
Strong overlap and usable reach. One of your first two or three.
- Missing: How you will judge it
- Lead sharing agreed, but the form does not state which companies receive a person's details. Never pass on contacts people did not agree to share.
- Lead sharing agreed with nobody named to follow up. Contacts go cold in days.
- Promotion agreed without dates. Uneven promotion is the most common way these fail.
- Work has already started on an unwritten agreement. Unspoken expectations turn into resentment by week three.
- 3 assets planned. One good asset promoted well beats five promoted by nobody.
Agree lead sharing in writing before anything goes live.
The crowd was large and almost none of it was your buyer. That is an overlap problem, and a different asset for the same list will not fix it.
- 400 sign-ups, 6 of them your buyer, no pipeline. That was a list-building exercise, not a partnership.
- You spent 6.7x the partner's hours. Promotion or production was not shared as agreed.
Small overlap partner — Do it again
Real pipeline from the right audience after a full sales cycle is the pattern worth repeating — consider a rhythm, such as one joint asset a quarter.
- Pipeline per hour of your effort: 8,182. Compare partners on this, not on raw sign-ups.
This is a rubric, not a prediction. Use your own numbers, not an industry benchmark.
